item.title: “‘The world is deficient, longing, a slave to craving’ — that, great king, is the fourth exposition of the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One,…
item.description:
“‘The world is deficient, longing, a slave to craving’ — that, great king, is the fourth exposition of the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, the Knower, the Seer, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One. Having known, seen, and heard that exposition, I went forth from the household life into homelessness.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 82 – Raṭṭhapālasutta
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, the Blessed One Vipassī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, thought: ‘This Dhamma that I have realized is deep, hard to see, hard to…
item.description:
“Monks, the Blessed One Vipassī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, thought: ‘This Dhamma that I have realized is deep, hard to see, hard to awaken to, peaceful, sublime, beyond the sphere of logic, subtle, to be understood by the wise. But this generation delights in sensual pleasures, is devoted to sensual pleasures, is fond of sensual pleasures. For a generation that delights in sensual pleasures, is devoted to sensual pleasures, is fond of sensual pleasures, it is hard to see this principle of specific conditionality (dependent origination); it is hard to see the principle that all formations are peaceful, that all substrates of rebirth are eliminated, that craving is destroyed, that there is dispassion, cessation, Nibbāna.’”

From: Dīgha Nikāya 14 – Mahāpadānasutta

item.title: “I do not see any other form, monks, that so obsesses and occupies the mind of a man as the form of a woman. The…
item.description:
“I do not see any other form, monks, that so obsesses and occupies the mind of a man as the form of a woman. The form of a woman, monks, obsesses and occupies the mind of a man.”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 1.1

item.title: Elder Parāpariya: “Having abandoned the six sense-bases, With sense-doors well restrained, Having pulled out the root of evil, I have attained the destruction of defilements.”
item.description:
Elder Parāpariya:
“Having abandoned the six sense-bases,
With sense-doors well restrained,
Having pulled out the root of evil,
I have attained the destruction of defilements.”

From: Theragāthā 1.116

item.title: Elder Tissa: “As if struck by a sword, As if his head were on fire, Mindful, a monk should go forth, Abandoning sensual lust.”
item.description:

Abandoning sensual lust.”

item.title: “Monks, the large deep lake refers to sensual pleasures. Monks, the great herd of deer refers to beings. Monks, the man who does not desire…
item.description:
“Monks, the large deep lake refers to sensual pleasures. Monks, the great herd of deer refers to beings. Monks, the man who does not desire their welfare, benefit, security refers to Māra the Evil One. Monks, the dangerous path refers to the wrong eightfold path – wrong view, wrong intention, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, wrong concentration. Monks, the male decoy refers to delight and greed. Monks, the female decoy refers to ignorance. Monks, the man who desires their welfare, benefit, security refers to the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One. The safe, secure path leading to happiness refers to the Noble Eightfold Path – right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 19 – Dvedhāvitakkasutta

item.title: “So too, Māgandiya, contact with sensual pleasures in the past was painful, very hot, very feverish; contact with sensual pleasures in the future will be…
item.description:
“So too, Māgandiya, contact with sensual pleasures in the past was painful, very hot, very feverish; contact with sensual pleasures in the future will be painful, very hot, very feverish; contact with sensual pleasures in the present is painful, very hot, very feverish. And these beings who have not abandoned lust for sensual pleasures, being consumed by craving for sensual pleasures, burned by the fever of sensual pleasures, with corrupt faculties, perceive as pleasure that which is actually painful contact with sensual pleasures.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 75 – Māgandiyasutta

item.title: “If there is form, Rādha, then there is death, or a killer, or being killed. Therefore, Rādha, you should see form as death, see it…
item.description:
“If there is form, Rādha, then there is death, or a killer, or being killed. Therefore, Rādha, you should see form as death, see it as a killer, see it as being killed, see it as a disease, see it as a boil, see it as a dart, see it as misery, see it as its own misery. One who sees form thus sees rightly.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 23.1

item.title: Behold this adorned appearance, With jewels and earrings, A skeleton covered by skin, Made beautiful by clothes.
item.description:
Behold this adorned appearance,
With jewels and earrings,
A skeleton covered by skin,
Made beautiful by clothes.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 82 – Raṭṭhapālasutta

item.title: “What do you think, Māgandiya? Here, a person formerly was infatuated with forms cognizable by the eye that were desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with…
item.description:
“What do you think, Māgandiya? Here, a person formerly was infatuated with forms cognizable by the eye that were desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. After some time, having known as they actually are the origination, the passing away, the gratification, the peril, and the escape in the case of forms, he abandons craving for forms, removes the fever for forms, and dwells with craving cut off, with mind inwardly peaceful.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 75 – Māgandiyasutta
